title: Confronting Jewish terrorism is not an act of Jew hate
gist: Rusbridger defends UK foreign secretary Ed Miliband's sanctions on the occupied West Bank — imposed with 11 other countries — by citing a June 2026 letter from 200-plus former Israeli prime ministers, spy chiefs and IDF commanders warning of “Jewish terrorism” and ethnic cleansing. He argues critics who invoke the two-state solution while opposing every measure to preserve it must answer five questions that lead to either one state or permanent political inequality.

themes.theme: West Bank facts on the ground

insights.claim: Settlers treated the Gaza war as an opportunity and established dozens of new illegal outposts across the West Bank, starting each with one or two tents and a few cows or sheep before confiscating the surrounding land.
insights.speaker: Alan Rusbridger
insights.so_what: Documents a mechanised land-acquisition process running under cover of the Gaza war — the physical basis for annexation and for sanctions targeting.
insights.quote: The settlers realised that the war in Gaza is their opportunity, so they settled dozens and dozens and dozens of new, illegal outposts. You will see them on every hill.
insights.locator: We drove for an hour or so out of Tel Aviv

insights.claim: Haaretz columnist Gideon Levy, who has travelled to the West Bank weekly for 40 years, describes daily settler attacks — burning cars, fields, olive trees and houses, and periodically killing shepherds — with soldiers present protecting the settlers and in a few cases participating.
insights.speaker: Alan Rusbridger
insights.so_what: Alleged army complicity, not just settler violence, is what converts this into a state-responsibility question and therefore a sanctions question.
insights.quote: The West Bank is now a lawless place, unbelievable, and no Israeli knows anything about what’s going on here.

insights.claim: Most Israelis have little idea what has been happening in the West Bank because local media mostly turn a blind eye, and international journalists are routinely attacked while Israeli soldiers or police stand idly by.
insights.speaker: Alan Rusbridger
insights.so_what: An information gap inside Israel explains the divergence between Israeli domestic opinion and international reaction — relevant to how fast domestic political pressure can build.
insights.locator: Even most Israelis have little idea

insights.claim: A June 2026 letter from more than 200 former members of the Israeli establishment — including ex-prime ministers Ehud Barak and Ehud Olmert, former heads of Mossad and Shin Bet, former IDF chiefs, judges and generals — issued a “final warning” accusing Netanyahu's government of failing to confront “Jewish terrorism”.
insights.speaker: Alan Rusbridger
insights.so_what: When former security chiefs break ranks publicly, it signals elite fracture inside Israel and lowers the diplomatic cost of allied sanctions.
insights.locator: Then please read a June 2026 letter

insights.claim: The signatories said West Bank settler violence serves an ideology of “ethnic cleansing” designed to drive Palestinians from their communities and make eventual annexation possible, and Olmert subsequently called it an organised, systematic, state-funded campaign of ethnic cleansing and crimes against humanity.
insights.speaker: Alan Rusbridger
insights.so_what: Framing by former Israeli premiers gives legal-grade language to annexation risk, which is the trigger for wider EU/UK measures.
insights.quote: an “organised, systematic, state-funded campaign of ethnic cleansing and crimes against humanity”

insights.claim: Two former Israeli ambassadors, a former attorney general and a former Knesset speaker wrote to the Times welcoming the UK sanctions, arguing that distinguishing between Israel and settlements built in violation of international law is a defence of the two-state solution rather than hostility to Israel.
insights.speaker: Alan Rusbridger
insights.so_what: Establishes an Israeli-establishment endorsement of the settlement/Israel distinction — the legal architecture any broader sanctions regime would use.
insights.quote: distinguishing between Israel and the settlements built in violation of international law is not an act of hostility towards Israel. It is a defence of the two-state solution, and of the security of Israelis and Palestinians alike.
insights.locator: They were joined on Friday in a letter to the Times

insights.claim: UK foreign secretary Ed Miliband, along with 11 other countries, imposed a trade and financial cordon around the occupied West Bank, and was promptly accused of being anti-Jewish, hostile to Israel and stirring up antisemitism in the UK.
insights.speaker: Alan Rusbridger
insights.so_what: A 12-country coordinated economic cordon on the occupied territories is a material escalation for companies with settlement-linked supply chains.
insights.locator: And yet when UK foreign secretary Ed Miliband

insights.claim: The 12 countries were motivated not only by settler violence but by the expedited E1 settlement project east of Jerusalem, which would drive a wedge through the West Bank and which far-right minister Bezalel Smotrich has said is designed to “bury the idea of a Palestinian state”.
insights.speaker: Alan Rusbridger
insights.so_what: E1 is the specific, datable catalyst driving sanctions escalation — track its construction milestones as the trigger for further measures.
insights.quote: bury the idea of a Palestinian state
insights.locator: The 12 countries taking this action are alarmed

insights.claim: The UK Chief Rabbi called the sanctions “a dark day for British Jews” while also professing belief in Palestinian self-determination, an inconsistency the author uses to argue the domestic backlash is unreasoned.
insights.speaker: Alan Rusbridger
insights.so_what: Signals the domestic political cost the UK government is absorbing to hold this position, which bears on whether it is sustained.
insights.quote: a dark day for British Jews
insights.locator: The Chief Rabbi, swift to put the boot into Miliband

insights.claim: Mike Huckabee, the US ambassador to Israel, called the sanctions “irrational” and “discrimination against the Jewish people” and wrote that the Jew hate of the British government knows no boundaries and no facts.
insights.speaker: Alan Rusbridger
insights.so_what: Marks an open US–UK diplomatic rift over Israel policy, a divergence with consequences for allied coordination.
insights.quote: The Brits have lost it. The Jew hate of their government knows no boundaries and knows no facts.
insights.locator: Among those respectfully interviewed about this week’s sanctions

insights.claim: Huckabee is a self-identified staunch Christian Zionist who personally supports Israel annexing the West Bank, said in his 2008 presidential campaign that “There is no such thing as a Palestinian”, and rejects the concepts of a West Bank, a settlement and an occupation entirely.
insights.speaker: Alan Rusbridger
insights.so_what: The US ambassador's stated position is annexationist, which should be priced into expectations of US restraint on Israeli settlement policy.
insights.quote: I think Israel has title deed to Judea and Samaria
insights.locator: But I didn’t read or hear any interviewer giving any context on Huckabee

insights.claim: No interviewer supplied that context, which the author treats as a broader failure of journalism to interrogate the assumptions of sanctions opponents.
insights.speaker: Alan Rusbridger
insights.so_what: Media framing gaps are why annexationist positions circulate as neutral diplomatic commentary.
insights.quote: A relevant piece of context, no? This is not any ordinary ambassador.
insights.locator: A relevant piece of context, no?

insights.claim: The proposed test for anyone opposing settlement sanctions while claiming to back two states is a five-question sequence: have you spoken against settlement expansion; do you back a sovereign Palestinian state; where would its territory be at current expansion rates; if a viable state becomes impossible should Palestinians get Israeli citizenship and an equal vote; and if not, what permanent political rights do they have?
insights.speaker: Alan Rusbridger
insights.so_what: A reusable interrogation framework that forces stated positions on Israel/Palestine into one of two terminal outcomes — useful for reading any politician's real position.
insights.locator: So here are five questions I think journalists should ask

insights.claim: Question four is the decisive one: answering yes to Israeli citizenship and an equal vote amounts to the one-state solution whether or not it is called that, while answering no makes the issue permanent political inequality — or, as one might call it, a form of apartheid.
insights.speaker: Alan Rusbridger
insights.so_what: Collapses the ambiguity most Western politicians rely on; the rhetorical middle ground is shown to be untenable, which is why sanctions politics will keep escalating.
insights.quote: Or, as one might call it, a form of apartheid.
insights.locator: Question four is the tricky one.

insights.claim: The “autonomy” answer fails the same test, because if Israel controls borders, airspace, security, immigration, foreign relations, natural resources and ultimate legislative authority, autonomy does not solve the sovereignty question.
insights.speaker: Alan Rusbridger
insights.so_what: A checklist for evaluating any proposed Palestinian autonomy arrangement announced in negotiations.
insights.locator: If the answer is “They will have autonomy”

insights.claim: Support for the two-state solution becomes merely declaratory when its advocate opposes virtually every available measure intended to prevent the territorial conditions for it from disappearing.
insights.speaker: Alan Rusbridger
insights.so_what: Distinguishes stated from revealed preference in Western Israel policy — the gap that sanctions decisions now expose.
insights.locator: At what point does support for a two-state solution become merely declaratory
